overview: The Haudenosaunee are a continuing confederacy of nations. The Onondaga Nation's own accounts describe government, food, ceremonies and wampum as living practices connecting community responsibilities with historical memory.

items.text: Clan Mothers select the Hoyane who represent their clans in council. They can remove a leader who fails to represent the clan, after warnings.
Wampum makers cut, round, sand and drill shell beads. Woven strings and belts support the remembrance of agreements and their histories.
Wampum strings can carry invitations to council meetings. They also identify leadership titles and give weight to a speaker's words.
Corn, beans and squash are the Three Sisters. Onondaga food traditions also include fishing, hunting, gathering and sharing food within the community.
The Thanksgiving Address opens gatherings by acknowledging people, the natural world and their interdependence. Speakers express it in their own words.
Clan Mothers help sustain ceremonies and teach younger generations. These are present-day responsibilities, not customs of a vanished society.
